title: Herdr executor C: enforce the wall clock, or refuse the bound at dispatch
description:
Enforce the wall clock. Noticing a deadline and enforcing one are different
jobs, and Phase 1 splits them across exactly this seam.

INHERITED, do not re-implement: the settlement deadline is reconciler-side
(dispatch.go:971 — issued + WallSeconds + the wipe threshold), so a herdr worker
that goes quiet is declared settled on schedule exactly as a local one is. The
bound reaches the executor as spec.Limits.WallSeconds (dispatch.go:717, default
3600 — "an unbounded job is one nothing stops", reconcile.go:38-39).

NOT INHERITED: the kill. Phase 1's executor enforces the bound because it owns
the process it started (subprocess/inspect.go:131, collect.go:177). A herdr
worker's process belongs to HERDR. Nothing inherited stops it, so the reconciler
would declare the attempt settled and move on while the agent keeps running and
keeps spending — with the run's own records agreeing it is over. That is worse
than no bound, because the operator believes in it.

Do:
- Stop the agent through herdr when spec.Limits.WallSeconds is reached, and
  record it as STOPPED AT ITS WALL CLOCK rather than merely settled. Phase 1
  already distinguishes those two verdicts; keep them distinct.
- If the bound cannot be enforced through the herdr protocol available, that is
  a REFUSAL AT DISPATCH naming the bound and the herdr version — never a
  promise. A limit nothing enforces is a limit the operator trusts wrongly.
- A stop at the wall clock says nothing about the WORK. It settles the attempt;
  the branch and the report are still read the usual way (tick 2xu owns that).

Builds on tick 3gv.
